title: Digital Courts Initiative: What Advocates Need to Know
author: B. Ramakrishna Rao
excerpt: The AP e-Courts project enters Phase III with mandatory e-filing and a dedicated advocate portal — here is what every member must do before 30 September 2026.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh e-Courts project has entered its third phase, with the Krishna District Court slated for full digital integration by December 2026. Key changes include mandatory e-filing for all civil suits above ₹5 lakh, real-time case-status notifications via SMS, and a dedicated advocate portal for cause list management.

The Association's Technology Committee has been in dialogue with the District Judge's office to ensure a smooth transition. Members are encouraged to register their bar enrollment number on the AP eCourts portal before 30 September 2026 to avoid delays when the mandatory phase begins.

Training workshops will be organised at the Bar Association Hall in September. Watch the News & Events page for dates and registration details.

title: Legal Aid Camp at Ibrahimpatnam: A Report
author: K. Sarada Devi
excerpt: The free legal aid camp held on 5 May 2026 saw over 300 villagers receive guidance on land rights, family disputes, and pension matters.
content:
The Bezwada Bar Association, in collaboration with the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), conducted a free legal aid camp at the Ibrahimpatnam Municipal Hall on 5 May 2026. A team of twelve advocates from the Association attended, covering a range of legal areas.

Key highlights:

  • 326 villagers received free legal consultation
  • 47 cases referred to the DLSA for ongoing pro bono representation
  • Land rights and patta disputes: 38% of cases
  • Family matters — maintenance and domestic violence: 29%
  • Pension, MGNREGS, and government scheme grievances: 21%
  • Other civil matters: 12%

The camp was inaugurated by the Additional District Judge, Krishna, and was widely covered by local media. The Association extends its gratitude to all participating advocates for their time and commitment to access to justice.

title: Constitution Day Seminar 2026: Highlights
author: P. Venkata Subrahmanyam
excerpt: Over 400 advocates attended the annual Constitution Day seminar on the theme of judicial independence and the evolving role of the bar.
content:
The annual Constitution Day Seminar was held on 26 January 2026 at the Bar Association Hall, Governorpet. The theme this year was "Judicial Independence and the Role of the Bar."

The seminar was chaired by the President of the Bezwada Bar Association and featured the following speakers:

  • Chief Guest: Hon'ble Sitting Judge, AP High Court
  • Sri Ch. Venkateswara Rao, Senior Advocate & Former Advocate General, AP
  • Dr. B. Madhava Reddy, Professor of Law, Nagarjuna University

Key points from the discussion included the importance of bar associations in safeguarding judicial independence, the constitutional mandate for legal aid under Article 39-A, and the evolving role of technology in access to justice.

A souvenir was released at the event, containing scholarly articles by members. Copies are available at the Association office.
